newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SPEED SKATING-GERMANY'S SCHENK CLOSES IN ON TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-GERMANY'S SCHENK CLOSES IN ON TITLE.

text.p: German speed skater Franziska Schenk moved a step closer to securing her first overall World Cup title with a second placing in the 1000 metres in the penultimate competition of the season on Saturday.

Schenk, who has won five races this season over 1,000 metres, posted a time of one minute 21.27 seconds, 0.19 seconds behind winner Marianne Timmer of the Netherlands and 0.46 ahead of American Chris Witty.
Three weeks after clinching world championship gold in Hamar, Norway, Schenk's hopes of also lifting the overall 500 metres title suffered a setback when she crashed in her race.
The 22-year-old suffered bruising when she lost control on the first corner to lose her overall lead in the distance's World Cup standings to Ruihong Xue of China.
Xue posted a winning time of 40.40 seconds on the course which hosted the 1976 Olympics, ahead of Timmer in 40.45 and China's Jin Hua in 40.70.
Schenk must win at the March 22-23 finals in Inzell, Germany, to snatch the overall title from Xue.
In the men's competition, Norway's Adne Sondral won the 1000 metres in 1:14.22 ahead of Jan Bos of the Netherlands and Canada's Kevin Overland.
Japanese racers made it a clean sweep in the 500 metres with Junichi Inoue posting the quickest time of 36.85. Manabu Horii was second and Hiroyasu Shimizu third.
